title: Disjointness away from the special coordinate
statement: Let $\omega$ be a sample of the hard distribution on $n$ coordinates, with special coordinate $T$, and let $i$ be any coordinate with $i \neq T$. Then Alice's bit and Bob's bit at coordinate $i$ are never both equal to $\mathrm{true}$; that is, it is not the case that both the Alice-bit at $i$ and the Bob-bit at $i$ hold.
hypotheses_covered: coordinate $i$ distinct from the special coordinate $T$ ($i \neq \omega.T$)
replaced: Away from $T$, generated coordinate-pairs are disjoint.
